Documentation → Tools & Studio → Studio security model

What Plugin Studio code cannot do to SATOM

How scripts, the console, apps and connections are kept from reading SATOM's secrets, changing its data or exhausting the node — jails, cgroup limits, destination checks, bounded templates and run caps — and what stays the administrator's job.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library studio.python_console
📍 WherePlugin Studio (first level of the sidebar)

What is it?#

Plugin Studio runs code and diagrams that administrators write, for operators to use. This page is the model that keeps that code away from SATOM itself. It was checked by a security review and an adversarial test on a running node (2026-10-20); every rule is pinned by a test.

What does it do?#

Property What protects it
Confidentiality Scripts and the console run in a bubblewrap jail with none of SATOM mounted — no .env, database socket, keys or other processes. The scripts runner has no database and no encryption key. A connection's secret reaches a run only as a single-use vault token unwrapped outside the jail. A connection never dials this node, the other HA node, loopback, link-local (cloud metadata) or reserved addresses. Changing where a connection points clears its secret. An answer that echoes the credential is masked. Operators see an app's outputs, not its step details.
Integrity No SQL or DDL reaches SATOM's database from Studio: data stores are checked JSON rows. A device change from an app is a draft change request that waits for approval. A PostgreSQL step runs one statement, read-only unless allowed. A value in an API path cannot leave its segment. An action runs once per run, on the version that produced it.
Availability The scripts and hooks runners have cgroup limits — 1 GiB memory, 256 tasks, two CPUs, a 512 MB memory /tmp — so no run can fill the disk or take the database's memory. The jail's root is read-only and its output is read with a cap. The console has no writable path, 512 MiB per process, a small task headroom and one run at a time. App runs are capped (2 per user, 8 per node), templates are bounded, HTTP calls have one total deadline, query results stop at 8 MiB, data stores have size limits, the scripts queue holds 50 runs, request bodies are capped.

Requirements#

Nothing to switch on: the limits ship in the units and the code. A site that needs more for its scripts raises them in a drop-in: systemctl edit satom-scripts.service.

Permissions#

  • studio.script_library writes scripts, connections, data stores and apps that run with the connections' credentials — grant it as you would an administrator's.
  • studio.python_console runs throwaway code over curated, masked data only.

How to use#

  • Use read-only credentials on external systems wherever a script or app only reads: a REST API admin with a read-only profile, a read-only database role. "Read only" in a PostgreSQL step is SATOM's guard; the role on the remote database is the real boundary.
  • Re-enter a connection's secret after changing its address — SATOM clears it on purpose.

Troubleshooting#

"the scripts queue is full (50 runs waiting)"#

Runs are waiting for the runner (four at a time). Wait for some to finish.

"you already have 2 app runs in progress"#

A user runs at most two apps at once; the node at most eight.

"template refused by the sandbox: an exponent above 64 is refused"#

Template arithmetic is bounded; compute large numbers in a script.

"a path cannot carry an encoded . / or \ (%2e %2f %5c)"#

A value in an API path held a slash or a dot-dot. Pass it as a query parameter instead (Query string (JSON)).

"the console is busy"#

One console run at a time per node; try again in a moment.

Related articles

Script LibraryKeep Python scripts with a form that operators fill in — write, test and publish them in a small in-browser editor; every run is sandboxed by a runner with no database access.Python ConsoleRun your own Python over curated, read-only fleet datasets inside a locked-down sandbox — for one-off reports and checks that no built-in page answers.ConnectionsName an external API or PostgreSQL database once, with its credential kept in the vault, for app steps and Script Library scripts to call — every call stays under the connection's base URL and never reaches this node or cloud metadata.Plugin Studio appsBuild a small application — a form, a diagram of steps over data stores, APIs, databases and scripts, and an output with actions — and publish it as its own entry in Operations → Plugins for the ADOMs and the groups or people you pick.Data storesDefine your own tables in Plugin Studio — typed columns, rows you edit by hand or from apps, filters and CSV in and out — with no SQL and no access to any other SATOM table.Plugin Studio examplesInstall working examples of every Plugin Studio piece with one click — a FortiGate policy finder built from the diagram, a NetBox IP owner script, a flow explainer with two connections, and data-store apps that work with no external system.
